3: A browser-based track builder racer. Sketch a closed circuit with a mouse or a fingertip, and APEX INK paves it into a 3D world with kerbs, run-off, scenery, and a full grid of AI rivals. Then race it.

5: ## Play

7: ```bash
8: npm install
9: npm start          # http://localhost:3000

29: - Freehand circuit drawing with live length, corner, straight, and run-off analysis.

#!/usr/bin/env bash
set -euo pipefail
cd "$(dirname "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")"

PROJECT_DIR="$(pwd -P)"
DIST_DIR="$PROJECT_DIR/dist"
WEB_DIR="${OPENCODE_WEB_DIR:-/home/runner/work/_temp/omgithub-web}"
PORT="${PORT:-3000}"
export PORT

now_ms() { date +%s%3N; }

run_timed() {
  local label="$1"
  shift
  local start end status=0
  start="$(now_ms)"
  "$@" || status=$?
  end="$(now_ms)"
  printf '[timing] %s: %d ms\n' "$label" "$((end - start))"
  return "$status"
}

install_dependencies() {
  if [[ -f package-lock.json ]]; then
    npm ci --no-audit --no-fund
  else
    npm install --no-audit --no-fund
  fi
}

write_deployment_output() {
  mkdir -p "$WEB_DIR"
  node -e '
    const { writeFileSync } = require("node:fs");
    const [output, project, directory] = process.argv.slice(1);
    writeFileSync(output, JSON.stringify({ project, directory }) + "\n");
  ' "$WEB_DIR/deployment-output.json" "$PROJECT_DIR" "$DIST_DIR"
}

[[ "$PORT" =~ ^[0-9]+$ ]] || { echo "PORT must be a number, got: $PORT" >&2; exit 1; }

if [[ ! -d node_modules/three ]] || [[ package-lock.json -nt node_modules/.package-lock.json ]]; then
  run_timed "install dependencies" install_dependencies
else
  printf '[timing] install dependencies: skipped (node_modules up to date)\n'
fi

# Build a self-contained static directory. The project serves prebuilt files and
# needs no runtime framework, so a clean copy is the build step.
run_timed "clean static build" rm -rf "$DIST_DIR"
run_timed "create static build" mkdir -p "$DIST_DIR"
run_timed "copy static files" cp -R index.html styles.css src vendor assets "$DIST_DIR"/
run_timed "verify static build" test -f "$DIST_DIR/index.html"

run_timed "write deployment-output.json" write_deployment_output

printf '[timing] serve: starting static server on port %s from %s\n' "$PORT" "$DIST_DIR"
cd "$DIST_DIR"
exec /usr/bin/time -p node ../server.mjs
#!/usr/bin/env bash

## Objective
- Add randomized team-radio pit calls and functional mid-race pit stops to the existing racing game, with the requested lap-based call schedule.

## Requirements
- No pit stop for 1- or 2-lap races.
- Call the player in after starting lap 2 for 3–4 laps, lap 3 for 5–6, lap 4 for 7–8, and lap 5 for 9–10.
- Show a popup at the top with randomized pit-call phrasing and make the pit stop work.

## Decisions
- The pit stop is mandatory for the player; AI behavior remains unchanged.
- Pit entry and limiter control are automatic after the call, matching the game's auto-throttle model.
- Tyres wear during the race; servicing replaces them and restores grip.

- Added randomized team-radio calls and the specified lap schedule.
- Implemented automatic pit approach, pit lane entry, Box 07 service, and rejoin.
- Added tyre wear/grip effects, tyre status HUD, mobile status display, and radio/service audio cues.
- Updated README pit-stop feature summary.
- Validated syntax, diff whitespace, simulated races, and desktop/mobile screenshots.

- Improve the garage models beyond plain white blocks.

- Apply pit stops to AI racers as well as the player.
